title: Keel: one governed endpoint that lets AI agents use a SaaS product
excerpt: Keel makes a SaaS product usable by AI agents. It reads the product's API, UI and docs, turns every operation into a typed, named tool on a hosted MCP server, and puts one endpoint in front of them with scopes, guardrails and approval gates. Every call is traced and can be replayed. webvise designed and built Keel in-house, without a client.
challenge: SaaS products are built for people. A button, a modal or a help article works for someone who can see and click. Adding an API does not close the gap, because an agent still cannot tell which calls are safe, whose permission it acts with, or what just happened. A single API key gives an autonomous caller all rights or none. And an agent that acts without a record leaves nothing to review or roll back. Keel asks how an existing product can be opened to agents without rebuilding it.
solution: Keel has two screens. The landing page explains the problem and the loop behind the product: map, generate, guard, publish and observe. The loop runs on every change, so the tools an agent sees always match the product. The operator console shows live call metrics and the typed tool schema Keel writes for each operation. It also shows the hosted MCP server, which Keel regenerates whenever the product changes, the scopes of each tool, the rate and spend limits, and the approval gates on every call that changes data. Every call leaves a trace that can be replayed. Connectors bring in the products a team already runs, such as GitHub, Linear, Notion, Slack and Stripe. Keel turns each into typed tools behind one endpoint, and an agent signs in once. No call that changes data reaches a product before it passes its scope and its approval gate. The interface is dark, with animated beams between the connectors, and is built in Next.js 16.
